neighbours.label: the word right after 'reason(s)' or 'led <someone>' that introduces grounds for a belief ('reason to believe', 'reason for', 'led scientists to assume'), as against 'to' after other nouns and verbs and 'reason' used as a subject
fire: After reading the letters, the historian had reason to doubt the official story.
Doctors now have strong reasons to suspect a link with diet.
Given the falling sales, there is little reason to expect a recovery.
The early data led many economists to believe inflation was over.
Neighbours had good reason to fear another flood that spring.
Her silence gave the detective reason to think she knew more.
Voters have every reason to question the new budget figures.
The faulty readings led engineers to conclude the pump had failed.
quiet: After reading the letters, the historian had time to visit the archive.
Doctors now have new tools to measure the effects of diet.
Given the falling sales, the shop plans to close in June.
The early data helped many economists finish their reports.
Neighbours had a chance to meet the mayor that spring.
Her silence made the detective want to leave the room.
Voters have the right to see the new budget figures.
The reason the pump failed was a cracked valve.
